key_insight: The paper presents a deterministic way to “draw” arbitrary 2D and 3D shapes on a water surface by combining focused transient waves with curve parametrization and amplitude correction.
engineering_relevance: This enables more precise wave-field control for ocean engineering, with potential uses in experimental basin testing, wave manipulation, and shape-specific surface generation.
method: Represent target shapes with B�e9zier curves or 3D geometry
Sample points at equal arc length to place wave foci consistently
Use Iterative Amplitude Correction (IAC) to reduce overshoot and improve superposition
evidence_signal: The approach was validated with linear wave theory, SPH simulations, and physical FloWave basin experiments that reproduced targets such as a 2D star and 3D pyramid.
watch_item: Accuracy may degrade at higher amplitudes because the method currently relies on linear theory and will need nonlinear wave modeling for stronger waves.
